status_changes.description: Host header is mandatory in every HTTP/1.1 request
status_changes.rationale: Directly supported by HTTP/1.1 specification documentation cited in evidence. This is a well-established RFC requirement.

status_changes.description: Content-Length or Transfer-Encoding must be present when request has a body
status_changes.rationale: Directly supported by HTTP/1.1 specification documentation. This is a fundamental requirement for message framing in HTTP/1.1.

status_changes.description: POST, PUT, PATCH requests should include Content-Type header with body
status_changes.rationale: Supported by specification documentation. While 'should' rather than 'must', it is a strong normative recommendation in the spec for proper content negotiation.

status_changes.description: HEAD response must not include a body
status_changes.rationale: Directly supported by HTTP/1.1 specification. This is a clear normative requirement.

status_changes.description: OPTIONS * is a server-level options request where path equals asterisk
status_changes.rationale: Supported by specification documentation describing the OPTIONS method with asterisk path for server-wide options.

status_changes.description: Requests must follow the sequence: METHOD /path HTTP/1.1, then headers, then optional blank line, then optional body
status_changes.rationale: Directly supported by HTTP/1.1 request format specification. This describes the canonical request structure.
